newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index edges higher on low volumes.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index edges higher on low volumes.

text.p: The Slovak SAX index edged up 0.02 points at 201.95, on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday, as dealers sensed a new spark in activity in the thin market.
Some brokers were quick to point out that volumes were still below a level that they considered satisfactory, but others said that trading had been thinner before.

"In principle blue chips are rising, and trading has become more lively as currently higher interbank money market rates had attracted some foreign capital inflow," Vladimir Kuklis, a CSOB Bank analyst, told Reuters.
"It appears that the trend will continue for a while."
The session's biggest gainer, drug producer Slovakofarma boosted the index with a 226 crown rise to 5,200, on 167 shares traded, after news of a positive earnings outlook.
Steel maker VSZ led the bourse volume-wise with 784 shares traded, firming two crowns to close at 697.
Oil refinery Slovnaft gained 10 crowns to close at 910 crowns.
Overall volume eased to 519,643 shares, from 620,979 million shares traded on Wednesday, while turnover eased to 435.88 million crowns, from 733.86 million.
